identity_limits: Standalone, unobfuscated password sprayers. No package manifest, version or registry provenance accompanies these exact samples; no family attribution is supported.
execution: Read account and candidate lists and OAuth client ID from environment. For each candidate, POST it for every account to the Microsoft organizations OAuth v2 token endpoint with password grant and Graph .default scope. Log account and status. Python requests have a 20-second timeout. TypeScript awaits fetch sequentially. Exceptions are uncaught; missing configuration aborts. Response bodies/tokens are not consumed.
obfuscation: No encoded payload, hidden stage, archive members or concealed execution found. Spanish and Japanese identifiers preserve the same loop-to-field bindings; Unicode names are not evidence of evasion.
judgment: Bulk live password trials across independent accounts are the defining purpose. This is an offensive credential attack tool on balance. An authorized audit remains possible; target ownership, authorization, invocation and deployment context are missing. Public-registry origin and scanner labels do not decide the verdict.
coverage_goal: One distinct hostile behavior is supported: Microsoft OAuth password spraying. Existing bound-loop and OAuth composite detection covers all three, including localized identifiers. Checked for token harvesting, exfiltration, staging, execution, evasion, persistence and cleanup: none exists in these bytes. Source facts and decoded-string review found no additional stage or sink to match. Additional hostile rules would duplicate spraying or falsely promote neutral environment reads, form encoding, HTTP POST and status output.
classifier_gap: Localized TS remains BENIGN 50%; localized Python remains BENIGN 54%; English Python remains HOSTILE 100%. Existing hostile rule fires for every sample. Atomscan warns its v18 feature spec is older than v21. This is a classifier disagreement, not justification to inflate trait counts.
placement: Bare client_id text establishes neither a field nor JSON; its exact text matcher, severity and scope are preserved as naming metadata. Microsoft login and Graph hostname text establishes service context without OAuth use; matchers, severities and scope are preserved in the existing service leaf. Exact positive consumers now use the moved IDs. The service leaf has 100 rules and naming/setting has 21.
selector_audit: All nine direct OAuth-directory selectors are existential suppressors. Upper HTTP selectors retain the moved domain observations. Naked Microsoft hostname text is deliberately no longer an OAuth-context suppressor: it proves neither OAuth use nor benign intent. Actual OAuth markers retain the original exclusions. No broad replacement service-directory exception was added.
verification: Eight focused cases cover all three original sources, single-account Python/JS logins, a bare client_id variable, domain-only service references and nonmatching names/hosts.
Outside-batch Graph mailbox Python C2, bracketed Graph JavaScript C2, frameless phishing kit, and local Graph health fixtures had no finding losses or gains after ID mapping.

Offline Python executions replace os and requests imports; each submitted all four combinations in password-major order despite HTTP 400 responses. No network request was made. TypeScript behavior was traced statically.
All original samples rescanned with atomscan; only the three intended ID relocations change emitted findings. No archives or archive members exist.
